title: Part (a): high-probability lower bound (the log(1/δ) and k/ε in probability) not proved

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Severity: gap (sharpness claim).** The abstract/summary assert the *sharp* high-probability threshold $\ell=k+\Theta((k+\log\frac1\delta)/\varepsilon)$. Only the **upper** direction is proved (Thm. `thm:hp`). Thm. `thm:lower` establishes sharpness of the constant $1+\frac{k}{p-1}$ **in expectation only**.

There is no lower bound showing that, in the *high-probability* sense, the $\log(1/\delta)$ dependence (nor the $k/\varepsilon$ in probability rather than in expectation) cannot be reduced. Thus the "$\Theta$" in the high-probability statement is unjustified.

**Suggested fix.** Add an anti-concentration / Gaussian small-ball lower bound: on the flat-tail family $A_{\beta,d}$, lower-bound the $(1-\delta)$-quantile of $\|\Sigma_2\Omega_2\Omega_1^\dagger\|_F^2/\tau_k^2$ by $\gtrsim\frac{k+c\log(1/\delta)}{p}$, using independence of $\Omega_1,\Omega_2$ and a Gaussian lower-tail estimate.
